more-is-not-safer.description: stating all requirements at once lowered compliance (98.7% for one requirement alone against 85.0% for gpt-4o with 19) [1], and repository context files that restated discoverable information did not generally improve coding-agent success [2].

written-requirements-reduce-variance.title: content-library research, Why do explicit written requirements reduce the variation in LLM output?

gloaguen-evaluating-agents-md.title: Gloaguen, Mündler-Sasahara, Müller, Raychev, Vechev, Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents? (v3, 2026-09-29)

human-manages-the-context.title: Human manages the context
human-manages-the-context.script: You run the bench. You manage what goes on it, and you steer the agent in the right direction. Think of the AI as a hire: how would you brief a brand new colleague on their first day, and what would you not bother them with?

not-how-the-ai-works-inside.title: Not how the AI works inside
not-how-the-ai-works-inside.script: The human manages two things: what lands on the bench, and where the work is heading. What happens inside the worker is not your job. That is why you can learn this today, without engineering knowledge. So what does a bench look like when it goes bad?
